caveats: The implementation is unverified; analysis is based on heimdall/evmole decompilation plus behavioural traces, not source review
USD values move with the ETH price (the extractable bound is aWETH-denominated); measured $22.33M-$22.50M across blocks 52,213,000-52,218,505
The full-equity fork test models the debt-token injection with deal() (production: swap borrowed aWETH -> USDC/cbBTC/EURC and transfer to the vault; DEX spread ~0.1-0.3% not modelled)

The residual/privileged amounts are not fresh-unprivileged extraction; they require the already-whitelisted helper/attacker key, one of the 33 whitelisted addresses, or a Safe threshold (3-of-7 / 3-of-8)

The working folder was externally wiped mid-run (2026-10-05 ~19:12) and restored from the CI snapshot and session records; on-chain state was re-measured after restoration and was unchanged (exposure still live)
Whether the attacker's key is still active is unknown; the capability is live regardless (helper still whitelisted)
No protocol has publicly claimed the vault; depositor/ownership structure is not fully determinable on-chain
one_liner: Fresh external unprivileged attacker can extract $0 from the Base vault (whitelist gate on borrow/withdraw/repay; helper owner-gated; copycat attempt reverted !W; independently re-probed across all selectors); the live exposure is the original attacker's still-whitelisted helper: $22.39-22.50M zero-capital (Aave HF bound) or $23.91M net via borrow->repay->borrow, plus equivalent privileged paths (owner Safe 3-of-7 is borrow-exempt; ProxyAdmin Safe 3-of-8 can upgrade), unrevoked since the Oct-4 $6M incident.
